name: Alien Hives
background:
The Alien Hives are a faction of aliens using biotechnology, made up of a variety of subspecies which come from the remote frontiers of the galaxy, hoping to recreate the Mother that shaped them.

When they first arrived, they were viewed as monstrous invaders, but after a long war of extermination, breakthroughs in communication led to a fragile peace. Now, the Hives must come to terms with the legacy of the First Contact War and decide how they are to adapt.
backgroundFull:
Born on the fertile but unstable world known as Ar’khsenos, the Alien Hives are made up of the species that specialised to survive the constant cycle of extinction on their world. This cycle would only find its end as an entity which they came to know as the Mother developed a way to transmit her memories into the various species of the Ar’khsenos.

These species lived together in harmony under her guidance for thousands of years in a period known as the Everbloom. This changed suddenly when the Mother died; the traumatic details of the event have largely been lost to time, but before she died, she gave the species of Ark’henos a final gift: seven massive creatures capable of travelling through space, each bearing one of her genetic offspring. These space-faring creatures came to be known as Hiveships, and her offspring were known as the Children.

Hivers travelled throughout the Frontier,seeking a world where one of the Children could flourish and grow to take the place of their lost Mother, but with little success. After centuries of failed efforts beyond the edge of charted space, their hopes were rekindled with the distant Radiance Cascade, which echoed the Mother’s dying cries in their ancestral memories. Many Hiveships set out for the Sirius Sector. Their arrival set off a series of conflicts with the factions there known as the First Contact Wars, as communication proved difficult and many assumed the Hives were hostile because of their alien appearance and nature. The Hivers soon were locked into a war of extermination with the various species of Sirius, which only concluded when the DAO Union discovered a means to communicate.

Peace provided its own challenges for the Alien Hives, as they soon found themselves confronted with several alien ideas and values that challenged the structure of their society. They strive to stand on equal footing with the other species of the Sirius Sector, protect their migratory routes and defend their seeded worlds. Some in the lower castes now demand new rights, undermining the harmonious working of their Hiveships, while certain Hive Lords still wage a long war against all the species of Sirius, fearing that the corrupting influence of outsiders might ultimately destroy their way of life completely.

How will your Hive adapt?

product.description: Assault Grunts have perhaps the shortest gestation period out of any Hiver, and as such make up a large portion of many Hive’s populations. Their species was refined throughout the violent First Contact War to give the Alien Hives the numbers necessary to face their numerous enemies in the Sirius Sector Assault Grunts fill many vital non-combat roles as well, assisting in every corner of the Hive.

These Grunts have wings that are thin, translucent, membranes pulsing with alien muscle, allowing them to dive from above and soar through the open sky. They relish opportunities to visit new worlds, putting their flight capabilities to good use as scouts as they serve as the eyes of the Hive.

Among Hivers, Spores are closely associated with the Mother, sometimes referred to poetically as “Mother’s gifts”. Originally serving as her means of communicating with the Hivers, her progeny have developed countless variations over the centuries of wandering through space, ranging in size from massive Spores, which could take root and blossom into buildings, to minuscule and pollen-like, capable of delivering glimpses of the Hive’s memories to even the smallest creatures.

Hivers born with swollen sacs of volatile fluid fused into their bodies are known as Shooter Grunts. These sacs can be compressed and ruptured on command, projecting streams of acidic bile, corrosive plasma, or burning jets that can even melt steel plating.

Even among the Hives, Soul-Snatchers are unique and tend to keep themselves apart from others. They serve as eyes of the Hive Lord, ensuring the functioning of their Hive and assisting wherever there is trouble.

Swarmers are small arthropod-like creatures that crawl, burrow, and coil in great numbers alongside the Alien Hives. They have no eyes, relying instead on their claws to detect subtle vibrations in the ground and their tri-forked tongues to trace subtle scents in the air. Though individually fragile, in great masses they become carpets of fangs, claws, and chitin, overwhelming their foes through sheer persistence.

Nearly twice the size of a human and clad in chitinous plating, Hive Warriors form the backbone of their society. Contrary to the warlike name bestowed upon them by the inhabitants of the Sirius Sector, Hive Warriors are considered among the most adaptable Hivers, able to fill a variety of roles as the need arises.

Among Hivers, Spores are closely associated with the Mother, sometimes referred to poetically as “Mother’s gifts”. Originally serving as her means of communicating with the Hivers, her progeny have developed countless variations over the centuries of wandering through space, ranging in size from massive Spores, which could take root and blossom into buildings, to minuscule and pollen-like, capable of delivering glimpses of the Hive’s memories to even the smallest creatures.

Slithering four-armed predators with four gleaming eyes, Ravenous Beasts are born out of a union of speed, strength, and terror. Though they possess some superficial similarities to Grunts, they are faster, larger, and far more deadly on the battlefield.

With bodies that operate as highly advanced chemical refiners, these creatures are known as Venom Beasts to the wider Sirius Sector. These Beasts are able to extract and store chemicals from anything they consume, concentrating them into everything from potent poisons to intoxicants.

Brawny warriors sheathed in armour-like carapace that conceals their vestigial eyes. Nerve clusters woven into their helm-like plating allow them to sense vibrations, heat, and psychic echoes with startling precision even in complete darkness. They serve as guards and protectors, both protecting Hive Lords on visits and watching over brood chambers. Many Hiver’s first living memories are of Hive Guardians watching over them, gently guiding their clutch as they emerged into the world.

Like their namesake, Synapse Beasts serve as vital connection and communication points for the Hive. They transmit the will of the Hive Lords throughout the Hiveship while relaying urgent news to the council, allowing swift communication and coordination between even less psychically adept Hivers. In larger groups, Synapse Beasts are capable of relaying information over vast distances, beyond their star system, assisting the Hive with long-distance communication.

After travelling through a swathe of the Frontier, the Alien Hives reached the Sirius Sector. Their arrival set off a series of conflicts with the factions in Sirius, as communication proved difficult and many assumed the Alien Hives were hostile because of their alien appearance and nature.

Tempering the most aggressive tendencies of the Hive Lords on Hiveship Ikhanoz’s council, Snatcher Lord Nisuv views cooperation as essential to the Hives’ prosperity in Sirius, an extension of the Mother’s teachings, saying that the best fights are the ones that never happen.

Snatchers are a peculiar species, even within the very diverse population of the Hives. Their psychic abilities and skill for infiltration has caused some to see them as untrustworthy or devious. However, Snatcher Lord Nisuv is a shining example of the opposite.

Prime Warriors embody the strength and determination of the Hive, guiding their fellow Hivers at the forefront of work and warfare. They are most easily spotted by their horns, which serve to amplify their psychic sensitivity, allowing them to pick up distant signals and pass on orders from the Hive Lords, even when operating far away.

Vradhez has served his Hive for a long time, first assisting the late Hive Lord, and now as the chief advisor to Prime Warrior Druzhak. As his scarred face can attest, he has fought in many battles and lost countless friends. He will go to any lengths and sacrifice anything for his people.

From Hiveships above, Invasion Spores plummet to a planet's surface like falling stars. Their membranes toughen during descent, hardening into armour that can withstand anti-air measures. As they land, they disgorge their cargo onto a new world. Often, the contents are Hivers eagerly rushing out to greet their new surroundings, whether as explorers, protectors, or conquerors.

As a Prime Warrior, Druzhak was destined from birth to focus on war, leaving existential questions to the Hive Lord who led his people. However, the Hive sustained terrible losses during its migration through hotly contested territories, and Druzhak found himself leading the survivors.

He is a fearless combatant who takes his duty towards his people extremely seriously. He has seen many battles and has the scars to prove it, but all the death and pain he has witnessed weighs heavily on his soul.

Despite his reputation as a brute, Troseis is an ingenious Prime Warrior, whose obsession with digestion led him to a bio-weapon known as the Bileburner. This is because he would eat so much of whatever material he could get his claws on that his body responded by developing incredibly fierce digestive fluids.

With the help of other fellow Hivers, Troseis managed to design the Bileburner, which can project streams of corrosive acid onto foes. This did not earn him a lot of popularity at the beginning, as he was assigned to the defense of the insides of Hiveship Okhredoz.

Slow and ponderous, Mortar Beasts are living artillery, reshaping the battlefield from a distance. They are among the lifeforms adapted to meet the challenges of war within the Sirius Sector, allowing the Hivers to meet the long-range weapons of outsiders.

Wading through ranks of enemy infantry, Flamer Beasts disgorge the volatile fluids stored on their backs to turn the battlefield into an inferno. Hiver myth often associates fire with destruction and death, giving Flamer Beasts a fearsome reputation among their kind as weapons of war.

product.description: An amalgamation of traits from various Hive species, Shadow Hunters represent the cutting edge of adaptation among the Hivers. Hunters are lithe with forelimbs that may be adapted to possess a variety of specialised and deadly claws. They prefer to operate under the cover of darkness, relying on their subtle senses; they can sense even the most subtle vibrations in the air and possess a greatly heightened psychic sensitivity, sensing thoughts like ripples in water.

weapons.name: Strafing Toxin Breath
weapons.label: Strafing Toxin Breath (9", A6, Blast(3), Bane)

product.description: Ksi’adoz belongs to Hiveship Voithsor, one of the most secretive that dwells deep within the Sirius Sector. Travelling silently across the dense, hostile environment of the Foreign Confines, Voithsor Hivers rely on stealth while shying from conflict and even contact. Instead, they seeded remote and hidden worlds, while harvesting discretely from backwater systems. The Voithsor Council has long held that their species’ best chance at survival is to be as close to invisible as possible.

A strain descended from the Carnivo-Rex, Toxico-Rexes are adapted to make use of the Hive’s respectable arsenal of poisons. Their long armored bodies are marked by several pustules, carrying a dizzying variety of venoms delivered through their barbed tails and whip-like tentacles, striking at foes with unerring precision.

Drawing upon the ancient apex predators of their long-lost homeworld, the Carnivo-Rex strains were developed as a means to counter the fearsome Dynasty Tanks and armoured divisions the Hivers encountered in the Sirius Sector. Its frame bristles with jagged spines and its thick tail smashes through defenses with ease. Four eyes glare with predatory focus, while its serrated fangs promise only ruin.

The Psycho-Rex combines the stature of the Rex strain with the vast psychic potential of the Synapse Beast. The potent psychic abilities for Psycho-Rexes rival those possessed by any Hiver, allowing them to project waves of psychic agony that can leave entire squads convulsing in pain, seal their own wounds, or influence seeded life in the surrounding area to hinder foes.

The Hive Lords are powerful beings, with four massive arms that can wield a variety of fearsome bioweapons. Upon first encounter, many outsiders mistook them for  towering brutes, controlling their Hivemates through force.

However, those outsiders were mistaken; the Hive Lords are designed to allow their powerful forms to withstand lengthy communion with their Hiveship’s Child. They serve as the stewards of their people’s most ancient memories and their precious hope for the future.

A mountain of living flesh, the Tyrant Great Beast is a being whose bulk shakes the earth with every step. Spines and armored plates bristle across his frame, sprouting into heavy growths that double as both shield and weapon. On the battlefield, these Great Beasts are unleashed where resistance is strongest. Their burrow-cannon blasts tunnels beneath enemy lines, fracturing fortifications from below. Unlike the more specialized Great Beasts, the Tyrant Beast is a generalist juggernaut, wielding an arsenal that allows him to dominate both at range and in close combat.

weapons.name: Toxin Blaster
weapons.label: Toxin Blaster (18", A6, AP(1), Blast(6), Bane)

product.description: With six powerful arms, rows of jagged fangs, and thick chitinous armour, Burrowers are built to reshape worlds. Their surprisingly agile limbs allow them to dig with terrifying speed, carving out tunnels large enough for even Hive Lords to pass through.

Hive Lord Drekhor is a legend amongst the Hives, standing as a testament to their grim determination and martial valor against near impossible odds. 

He is most famous for Drekhor’s Last Charge, the battle which firmly established the fame of Hiveship Makhradontos, of which it remains one of the most celebrated fights. Memories of Drekhor’s pride and grit are instilled in the minds of every newborn Makhradontos Hiver.

Living fortresses that lumber into place on the battlefield, an Artillery Great Beast has a neck like a tower and a body swollen with organic plating. Each of these Great Beasts proudly sports a colossal bio-cannon on their back, an organ capable of hurling across vast distances.

weapons.name: Bug-Spewer Bio-Artillery
weapons.label: Bug-Spewer Bio-Artillery (24", A9, AP(1), Blast(6), Indirect)

product.description: Despite their hulking size, Devourer Great Beasts move with their six limbs with an uncanny agility. Their hooked claws allow them to easily clamber up cliffs and any fortress walls too tall for them to simply step over.

weapons.name: Grasping Tongue
weapons.label: Grasping Tongue (9", A6, AP(1), Blast(3), Reliable, Assault)

product.description: Hive Titans serve as the living hammer of the swarm. His body rises to the size of a building, armored in plates that shift and grow to absorb punishment. Dozens of Grunts cling to his armored hide, leaping into battle as he advances, turning his very body into a fortress and a carrier all at once.

From Hiveships above, Invasion Spores plummet to a planet's surface like falling stars. Their membranes toughen during descent, hardening into armour that can withstand anti-air measures. As they land, they disgorge their cargo onto a new world.

Certain strains have been modified to latch onto the ground with clawed tendrils when they make impact. These Artillery Invasion Spores serve as strongholds and anchors at key strategic positions, spraying fire on any foes who dare approach.

Some Beasts find their purpose in carrying their kin, supplies, and valuable specimens encased in protective membranes on their armoured backs, protecting the precious cargo until they arrive at their destination. Their name originated from the mistaken belief of early Eternal Dynasty observers, who believed they were incubating newborn Grunts to release on the battlefield.

gains.name: Devourer Titan

product.description: The Devourer Titan is an even larger strain of the Devourer Beast, dwarfing its smaller cousin. Its immense appetite is one few Hives can sustain for long, often driving it to battle fury as it swipes aside enemy fortifications and formations in search of food, slicing through tank hulls like food packaging. Devourer Titans lack the subtlety of their smaller cousins, but few can doubt their effectiveness as predators.

product.description: A living storm that can blot out the sky, the Winged Titan embodies total dominance with wings that stretch wider than city streets. Bony spines line each membrane, slicing the air as they drive his bulk into soaring leaps and devastating dives.

gains.name: Grasping Titan

product.description: Towering above walls and fortifications, a Grasper Titan is a Hiver born for sieges. Their immense bodies are covered in layers of natural armour as dense as stone. Massive whip-like tongues lash from their maws, capable of snaring prey or tearing apart walls.

specialRules.name: Predator Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Predator. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Unwieldy
specialRules.description: Strikes last when charging.

specialRules.name: Imprecise
specialRules.description: Gets -1 to hit when attacking.

specialRules.name: Predator
specialRules.description: For each unmodified roll of 6 to hit when attacking, this model may roll +1 attack with that weapon. This rule doesn’t apply to newly generated attacks.

specialRules.name: Infiltrate
specialRules.description: Counts as having Ambush, but may be deployed anywhere over 3" away from enemy unit.

specialRules.name: Crossing Attack
specialRules.description: Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and roll X dice. For each 6+ the target takes one wound.

specialRules.name: Hive Bond
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have this rule, the first time they are attacked each round, they get +1 to Morale Test rolls.

specialRules.name: Precise
specialRules.description: Gets +1 to hit when attacking.

specialRules.name: Unique Hero
specialRules.description: Counts as having Hero, and this model may only be taken once per army.

specialRules.name: Regenerative Strength
specialRules.description: Place one token on this model when it ignores a wound. Once per round, when it’s this model’s turn to strike in melee, roll as many dice as tokens on it before attacking, unless this unit is Fatigued. For each 4+ the target takes one wound.

specialRules.name: Caster Group
specialRules.description: This model counts as having Caster(1).

specialRules.name: Retaliate
specialRules.description: When this model takes wounds in melee, the attacker takes X hits per wound taken.

specialRules.name: Rapid Charge
specialRules.description: This model moves +4" when using Charge actions.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Hive Bond
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Hive Bond, they always get +1 to Morale Test rolls from Hive Bond (instead of only the first time they are attacked each round).

specialRules.name: Ravage
specialRules.description: Once per round, when it’s this model’s turn to strike in melee, roll X dice before attacking, unless this unit is Fatigued. For each 6+ the target takes one wound.

specialRules.name: Increased Shooting Range Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get +6" range when shooting. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Furious Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Furious. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Regeneration Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Regeneration. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Hit & Run Fighter
specialRules.description: Once per round, this model may move by up to 3" after being in melee.

specialRules.name: Stealth Buff
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 nearest friendly units within 12", which gets Stealth once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Self-Destruct
specialRules.description: If this model is killed in melee, the attacking unit takes X hits. If this model survives melee, after both sides have finished attacking, it is immediately killed, and the enemy unit takes X hits.

specialRules.name: Entrenched
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have this rule, as long as they haven't moved during this round, enemy units shooting at them from over 12” away get -1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: Ignores Cover
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Cover.

specialRules.name: Spell Conduit
specialRules.description: Casters within 12" that are from other friendly units may cast spells as if they were in this model's position, and get +1 to casting rolls when doing so. Friendly casters may only use this rule if this unit isn't Shaken.

specialRules.name: Spell Resistance
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 6+ it is ignored. If the wounds were from a spell, then they are ignored on a 2+ instead.

specialRules.name: Cumbersome
specialRules.description: May only use Hold or Advance actions, but can’t shoot when moving.

specialRules.name: Piercing Target
specialRules.description: Once per game, during this model's activation, pick X enemy units within 18" and in line of sight of it, and place one token on them. Friendly units get AP(+1) on their weapons when attacking them.

specialRules.name: Precision Debuff
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which gets -1 to hit rolls when attacking once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Piercing Growth
specialRules.description: Place one token on this unit at the beginning of each round if it's on the table and isn't Shaken, up to a max. of four tokens. For every two tokens, models with this rule in this unit get AP(+1) on their weapons.

specialRules.name: Spawn
specialRules.description: Once per game, when this model is activated, you may place a new unit of X fully within 6" of it.

specialRules.name: Takedown Strike
specialRules.description: Once per game, when it's this model's turn to strike in melee, it may make X attacks at Quality 2+ with AP(2), Deadly(3), and Takedown.

specialRules.name: Surprise Attack
specialRules.description: Counts as having Infiltrate. The first time this unit is activated, pick one enemy unit within 6" in line of sight, and roll X dice. For each 2+ it takes one hit with AP(1).

specialRules.name: Ignores Regeneration
specialRules.description: This weapon ignores Regeneration.

specialRules.name: Crossing Strike
specialRules.description: Once per activation, when this model moves through enemy units, pick one of them and attack it with this weapon as if it was shooting. This weapon may only be used in this way.

specialRules.name: Fragment
specialRules.description: When attacking units where most models have Defense 4+ to Defense 6+, the target must re-roll successful unmodified Defense results of 4-6.

specialRules.name: Unpredictable Fighter
specialRules.description: When in melee, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead.

specialRules.name: Rapid Charge Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game moves +4" when using Charge actions. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Hive Bond Aura
specialRules.description: This model's unit and up to 2 nearest friendly units picked before the start of the game get Enhanced Hive Bond. If this model is killed, picked models that are deployed lose the rule.

specialRules.name: Furious Buff
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 nearest friendly units within 12", which gets Furious once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: Unpredictable Fighter Mark
specialRules.description: Once per activation, before attacking, pick up to 3 enemy units within 18" in line of sight, which friendly units gets Unpredictable Fighter against once (next time the effect would apply).

specialRules.name: No Retreat
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule fails a morale test that causes it to be Shaken or Routed, the test counts as passed instead. Then, roll as many dice as the number of wounds it would take to fully destroy it, and for each result of 1-3 the unit takes one wound, which can't be ignored.

specialRules.name: Valiant
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have this rule, the first time they are attacked each round, they get +1 to Morale Test rolls.

specialRules.name: Enhanced Valiant
specialRules.description: If most models in this unit have Valiant, they always get +1 to Morale Test rolls from Valiant (instead of only the first time they are attacked each round).

specialRules.name: Ambush
specialRules.description: Only deploys D3 rounds afters its wave, and at the start of the round it's placed within 6” of a random AI Goal.

specialRules.name: Hero
specialRules.description: AI units within 6” use the Villain’s Qua for Morale Tests if it’s better than their own, as long as the Villain isn’t Shaken.

specialRules.name: Caster
specialRules.description: Follows same rules as heroes, picking one random spell to cast, and spending all tokens to cast it when activated. If the chosen spell can’t be cast for any reason, then the model doesn’t cast.

specialRules.name: Furious
specialRules.description: When charging, unmodified result of 6 to hit deal 1 extra hit (only the original hit counts as a 6 for special rules).

specialRules.name: Regeneration
specialRules.description: When a unit where most models have this rule takes wounds, roll one die for each. On a 5+ it is ignored.

specialRules.name: Stealth
specialRules.description: When units where most models have this rule are shot from over 9" away, enemy units get -1 to hit rolls.

specialRules.name: AP
specialRules.description: Targets get -X to Defense rolls when blocking hits.

specialRules.name: Takedown
specialRules.description: This model may pick any model in the target unit as its individual target for this weapon's attacks, which is resolved as if it was a unit of [1]. Takedown attacks must be resolved before other weapons.

specialRules.name: Deadly
specialRules.description: Assign each wound to one model, and multiply it by X. Hits from Deadly must be resolved first, and these wounds don’t carry over to other models if the original target is killed.

specialRules.name: Defense
specialRules.description: This model gets +X to Defense rolls.

specialRules.name: Unpredictable
specialRules.description: When attacking, roll one die and apply one effect to all models with this rule: on a 1-3 they get AP(+1), and on a 4-6 they get +1 to hit rolls instead.
